scope.selection_rule: Validated baseline and expansion profiles plus the nine repaired integrations in validation/repaired_library. Only each explicit executable profile is supported.
scope.operation_count_note: Triangle and dynamic-triangle operations share a family; maximal-biclique enumeration and count-only operations also share a family.

build_once_run_many.execution_model: Compile and link the validated implementations once. Each later query invokes the same binary with an operation, backend, canonical graph JSON, parameters, and optional-output flags.
why: No C++ or CUDA compilation occurs per user query.
The command boundary is stable JSON input and JSON output.
The runtime list command reports which validated backends were compiled into the current binary.
A long-lived service can invoke this binary now and can later call the same C++ library in-process if process startup becomes material.

options.description: CUDA device IDs; current validated paths use the first ID unless their facade states otherwise.
Explicitly permit an undirected projection for an undirected operation.
Omit execution statistics from result JSON.
Write result JSON to a file; use - for stdout.

accepted: a JSON array of vertex IDs
an object with a left_partition array
a JSON array of update objects
an object with an updates array
triangle_updates.batch_semantics: EDTC applies every deletion before every insertion, matching the validated artifact.

auxiliary_input_formats.query_graph: A second canonical_edge_list_v1 JSON graph passed with --query-graph.
auxiliary_input_formats.motif_graph: Each --motif value is a canonical_edge_list_v1 JSON graph; its graph.id becomes motif_id.

operations.validated_profile: Maximal gamma quasi-cliques supported by cuQC; the general problem spec's maximum_size and maximal_only choices are not exposed.

operations.partition_rule: Every graph vertex absent from left_partition belongs to the right partition.

backend_constraints.graphminer: undirected induced motifs of size 3 or 4
backend_constraints.graphset: undirected non-induced motifs of size 3 or 4
backend_constraints.dumato: undirected induced motifs of size 3 or 4

operations.command: graphmine run graph-motifs --graph DATA.json --motif MOTIF.json --backend graphminer --induced --include-instances --pretty

operations.validated_profile: The gMatch adapter supports its validated non-induced structural/label matching profile; general declarative edge/vertex predicates are not exposed.
Directed ordered feed-forward triangle A->B, B->C, A->C with distinct vertices, stable event ordering, integer timestamps, and an inclusive max_time_span window.
Unweighted undirected modularity heuristic. Resolution, weighted mode, CPM, and exact optimality are not exposed by the validated adapters.
Exact unweighted undirected betweenness using TurboBC's ordered-pair, endpoint-excluding native quantity. Other centrality measures are not exposed.

operations.command: graphmine run connected-components --graph GRAPH.json --connectivity-mode weakly_connected|strongly_connected [--backend ecl-scc] [--timeout-seconds N]
graphmine run max-flow-min-cut --graph GRAPH.json --source ID --sink ID [--unit-capacity] [--backend ecl-maxflow] [--timeout-seconds N]
operations.validated_profile: directed, integer edge capacities, total capacity <= 1e9; no vertex capacities

operations.command: graphmine run linear-assignment --graph GRAPH.json [--backend hungarian-cuda] [--timeout-seconds N] (complete square minimum-cost perfect assignment, <=64 per side, integer costs 0..999)
operations.validated_profile: complete square minimum-cost perfect assignment; <=64 per side; costs integer 0..999; declared sides

operations.command: graphmine run transitive-closure --graph GRAPH.json [--backend gdlog] [--timeout-seconds N] (reflexive closure; <=1024 vertices)
operations.validated_profile: directed full reflexive materialized closure; <=1024 vertices; build_index=false

operations.command: graphmine run butterfly-counting --graph GRAPH.json [--backend graphminer|gamma-butterfly] (global count only; undirected bipartite graph)
operations.validated_profile: exact global count only; declared bipartite sides
Exact full k-truss decomposition of unweighted undirected input; loops removed and parallel edges collapse to the smallest typed external edge ID.
Exact unweighted edge density |E(S)|/|S| on a nonempty undirected graph. No fixed cardinality, minimum-size constraint, weighted objective, or higher-order clique-density mode.

operations.command: graphmine run maximal-biclique-counting --graph GRAPH.json [--backend mbe-gpu] (count only; attributes.side = left|right)
operations.validated_profile: Exact count of nonempty maximal bicliques on one GPU; every vertex declares attributes.side=left|right. Count only: no vertex-set enumeration, size filters, bitmap variant, or multi-GPU mode.

operations.command: graphmine run personalized-pagerank --graph GRAPH.json --seed-vertex ID --top-k N --restart-probability 0.2 [--epsilon 0.01] [--random-seed N]
operations.validated_profile: Approximate top-k outgoing PPR on a directed unweighted multigraph, one seed, explicitly requested restart probability 0.2, dangling mass returned to that seed. Epsilon controls sampling; error_bound=null and error_bound_certified=false. No exact/converged guarantee, weighted walks, multiple seeds, reverse edges, or seed exclusion.

Exact undirected group Steiner tree with checked edge/vertex certificate; 1..16 nonempty groups, nonnegative integer weights <=2^53-1, tree cost bound below 2^58. Parallel edges use the cheapest edge, with typed edge-ID tie break. Required terminals can be singleton groups. No hop or diameter constraint.

operations.command: graphmine run influence-maximization --graph GRAPH.json --diffusion-model independent_cascade --seed-set-size N [--sample-count 256] [--random-seed N]
operations.validated_profile: Approximate independent-cascade seed selection on a directed graph with explicit edge probabilities in weight. Independent holdout spread; guarantee_met=false. No certified approximation ratio/failure probability, linear threshold model, or physical multi-GPU execution.

spec.name: Maximal Clique Enumeration
spec.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph, enumerate every vertex set that forms a clique and is not a proper subset of another clique.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_clique_size
problem_inputs.description: Return only maximal cliques at least this large.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized cliques; a finite value permits an incomplete result.

required_outputs.name: cliques
required_outputs.description: Each returned vertex set is a distinct maximal clique meeting the size constraint.

required_outputs.name: returned_count
required_outputs.description: Number of materialized cliques.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: True only if all qualifying maximal cliques were enumerated.

optional_outputs.name: total_count
optional_outputs.description: Total qualifying clique count when enumeration completed or exact count-only continuation was performed.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate all inclusion-maximal complete vertex sets satisfying minimum_clique_size.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every materialized set must be exact; complete=true requires exhaustive enumeration.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: The same vertex set may appear only once.
solution_semantics.ordering: No clique or vertex ordering is semantically required.

validation_rules: Every pair of distinct vertices in each result has an edge.
No outside vertex is adjacent to every vertex in a returned clique.
For complete=true, results equal a trusted exhaustive oracle on tractable graphs.
edge_cases: An empty graph returns no cliques.
An isolated vertex is a size-one maximal clique when minimum_clique_size <= 1.
A complete graph has exactly one maximal clique containing all vertices.

spec.name: Maximum Clique
spec.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph, find a clique with the largest possible number of vertices.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: return_all_ties
problem_inputs.description: Return every maximum clique rather than one representative.

problem_inputs.name: known_lower_bound
problem_inputs.description: A valid known lower bound on the optimal clique size.

required_outputs.name: maximum_size
required_outputs.description: Cardinality of the best clique found.

required_outputs.name: cliques
required_outputs.description: One maximum clique, or all tied maximum cliques when requested.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether maximum_size has been proven globally optimal.

optional_outputs.name: upper_bound
optional_outputs.description: Best certified upper bound when optimal=false.

solution_semantics.objective: Maximize the number of vertices in a complete induced vertex set.
solution_semantics.exactness: An exact completed result must have optimal=true; interrupted solvers may return a feasible clique and certified bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Tied maximum cliques must be unique as vertex sets.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering is semantically required.

validation_rules: Every returned set is a clique.
Every returned clique has maximum_size vertices.
optimal=true is valid only when no larger clique exists.
edge_cases: An empty graph has maximum_size 0 and one empty solution conventionally represented by an empty clique list.
A nonempty edgeless graph has maximum_size 1.
A complete graph's unique maximum clique contains every vertex.

spec.name: k-Clique Counting and Enumeration
spec.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph and integer k, count or enumerate every complete vertex set containing exactly k vertices.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: k
problem_inputs.description: Required number of vertices in each clique.

problem_inputs.name: mode
problem_inputs.description: Whether to count cliques or materialize their vertex sets.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized instances in enumerate mode.

required_outputs.name: count
required_outputs.description: Number of k-cliques found; it is the total only when complete=true.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether the count and enumeration cover all k-cliques.

optional_outputs.name: cliques
optional_outputs.description: Distinct k-cliques when mode=enumerate.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_count
optional_outputs.description: Number of k-cliques containing each vertex.

solution_semantics.objective: Count or enumerate all size-k complete vertex sets.
solution_semantics.exactness: complete=true requires an exact exhaustive result.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each unordered vertex set is counted once.
solution_semantics.ordering: Vertex and result order are irrelevant.

validation_rules: Every enumerated set contains exactly k distinct vertices.
Every vertex pair in each result has an edge.
When complete=true, count matches the number of unique qualifying sets.
edge_cases: If k exceeds the vertex count, count is zero.
For k=2, every unique graph edge is a 2-clique.
A complete n-vertex graph contains n choose k k-cliques.

spec.name: Quasi-Clique Mining
spec.problem_statement: Find vertex subsets whose induced subgraphs satisfy a minimum internal-degree fraction, allowing dense groups that are not complete cliques.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: gamma
problem_inputs.description: Every selected vertex must have induced degree at least ceil(gamma * (|S|-1)).

problem_inputs.name: minimum_size
problem_inputs.description: Minimum vertices in a returned quasi-clique.

problem_inputs.name: maximum_size
problem_inputs.description: Optional upper bound on result size.

problem_inputs.name: maximal_only
problem_inputs.description: Return only qualifying sets not contained in a larger qualifying set.

required_outputs.name: quasi_cliques
required_outputs.description: Unique vertex sets with size, induced edge count, density, and minimum internal degree.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every qualifying result was found.

optional_outputs.name: count
optional_outputs.description: Number of qualifying results.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate induced vertex sets satisfying the gamma minimum-degree condition and size bounds.
solution_semantics.exactness: All reported sets must satisfy the threshold; complete=true means exhaustive enumeration.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each vertex set appears once.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering is required.

validation_rules: Recompute induced degree for every selected vertex.
Verify size bounds.
When maximal_only=true, no result is contained in a larger qualifying set.
edge_cases: gamma=1 reduces the condition to clique mining.
Disconnected sets normally fail for useful gamma values but connectivity is determined solely by the stated degree condition.
No result is returned when minimum_size exceeds the vertex count.

spec.name: Densest Subgraph
spec.problem_statement: Find a nonempty vertex subset maximizing total induced edge value divided by the number of selected vertices.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges by summing nonnegative weights; use unit weight when weight_mode=unweighted.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use unit edge values or nonnegative input weights.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_vertices
problem_inputs.description: Minimum permitted result size; values above one define a constrained variant.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether an approximation is permitted.

required_outputs.name: vertices
required_outputs.description: Selected nonempty vertex set.

required_outputs.name: density
required_outputs.description: Total induced edge value divided by selected vertex count.

required_outputs.name: induced_edge_value
required_outputs.description: Induced edge count or weight sum.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified solution-quality bound for an approximate result.

optional_outputs.name: induced_edges
optional_outputs.description: Edges with both endpoints selected.

solution_semantics.objective: Maximize induced_edge_value / |S| over permitted nonempty vertex sets S.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true; approximate mode must disclose its bound when known.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Return one optimum unless tied solutions are explicitly added later.
solution_semantics.ordering: Vertex order is irrelevant.

validation_rules: All induced edge values are recomputed from the normalized graph.
Reported density equals induced_edge_value divided by result size.
All edge weights are nonnegative in weighted mode.
edge_cases: An edgeless nonempty graph has density zero.
Multiple distinct subsets may attain the same optimum.
An empty input graph has no feasible nonempty solution.

spec.name: k-Core Decomposition
spec.problem_statement: Assign every vertex its largest k for which it belongs to the maximal induced subgraph whose vertices all have internal degree at least k.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: requested_k
problem_inputs.description: Optionally materialize the vertices and edges of one k-core in addition to the full decomposition.

required_outputs.name: core_number_by_vertex
required_outputs.description: Largest core order containing each vertex.

required_outputs.name: degeneracy
required_outputs.description: Maximum core number in the graph.

optional_outputs.name: requested_core_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Vertices whose core number is at least requested_k.

optional_outputs.name: requested_core_edges
optional_outputs.description: Edges induced by requested_core_vertices.

optional_outputs.name: peeling_order
optional_outputs.description: A valid order in which vertices were removed.

solution_semantics.objective: Compute the complete core decomposition and graph degeneracy.
solution_semantics.exactness: Core numbers and degeneracy are exact.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each input vertex has exactly one core number.
solution_semantics.ordering: Peeling order may vary while core numbers remain invariant.

validation_rules: Every vertex assigned core c belongs to the c-core.
No vertex belongs to a core with order greater than its reported core number.
The requested k-core equals vertices with core number at least k.
edge_cases: Isolated vertices have core number zero.
An empty graph has degeneracy zero and an empty map.
Every vertex in a complete n-vertex graph has core number n-1.

spec.name: k-Truss Decomposition
spec.problem_statement: Assign every edge the largest k for which it belongs to a maximal subgraph where each edge participates in at least k-2 triangles within that subgraph.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: requested_k
problem_inputs.description: Optionally materialize one k-truss in addition to the full decomposition.

required_outputs.name: truss_number_by_edge
required_outputs.description: Largest k-truss containing each normalized edge.

required_outputs.name: maximum_truss_number
required_outputs.description: Largest truss number assigned to any edge, or zero for an edgeless graph.

optional_outputs.name: requested_truss_edges
optional_outputs.description: Edges with truss number at least requested_k.

optional_outputs.name: requested_truss_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Endpoints of requested_truss_edges.

optional_outputs.name: initial_support_by_edge
optional_outputs.description: Triangle support before iterative peeling.

solution_semantics.objective: Compute the complete edge truss decomposition using the k-2 support convention.
solution_semantics.exactness: All truss numbers are exact.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each normalized edge has exactly one truss number.
solution_semantics.ordering: Edge removal order may vary while truss numbers remain invariant.

validation_rules: Every edge in a returned k-truss has support at least k-2 within that truss.
No edge belongs to a truss above its reported number.
Requested truss edges are exactly those with truss number at least requested_k.
edge_cases: Edges in no triangle have truss number two.
A triangle's three edges have truss number three.
An edgeless graph produces an empty map and maximum_truss_number zero.

spec.name: Maximal Biclique Enumeration
spec.problem_statement: Given a bipartite graph, enumerate complete bipartite subgraphs that cannot be extended by adding a vertex to either side.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops and collapse parallel edges.
Reject any edge whose endpoints are in the same declared partition.

problem_inputs.name: left_partition
problem_inputs.description: All vertices belonging to the left side.

problem_inputs.name: right_partition
problem_inputs.description: All vertices belonging to the right side.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_left_size
problem_inputs.description: Minimum selected vertices on the left.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_right_size
problem_inputs.description: Minimum selected vertices on the right.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized bicliques.

required_outputs.name: bicliques
required_outputs.description: Distinct objects containing left_vertices and right_vertices.

required_outputs.name: returned_count
required_outputs.description: Number of materialized bicliques.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every qualifying maximal biclique was enumerated.

optional_outputs.name: total_count
optional_outputs.description: Total qualifying bicliques when known exactly.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate all inclusion-maximal pairs (L,R) with every possible cross-partition edge present.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every returned pair must be exact; complete=true requires exhaustive enumeration.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each pair of unordered vertex sets appears once.
solution_semantics.ordering: Order within or among bicliques is irrelevant.

validation_rules: Partitions are disjoint and cover every endpoint used.
Every left result vertex is adjacent to every right result vertex.
No additional vertex can extend either result side while preserving completeness.
edge_cases: A graph with no cross-partition edges has no nonempty bicliques.
An isolated vertex belongs to no biclique under the nonempty-side convention.
A complete bipartite input has one maximal biclique containing both full partitions.

spec.name: Triangle Counting and Listing
spec.problem_statement: Count all unordered triples of vertices connected by all three possible edges and optionally list the triples or their per-vertex and per-edge participation counts.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: list_instances
problem_inputs.description: Materialize triangle vertex triples.

problem_inputs.name: include_per_vertex_counts
problem_inputs.description: Return triangle participation per vertex.

problem_inputs.name: include_per_edge_counts
problem_inputs.description: Return triangle support per edge.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum listed instances; it does not permit truncating the global count.

required_outputs.name: global_triangle_count
required_outputs.description: Exact number of distinct undirected triangles.

required_outputs.name: instances_complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every triangle instance was listed when listing was requested.

optional_outputs.name: triangles
optional_outputs.description: Unique three-vertex triangle instances.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_count
optional_outputs.description: Triangles containing each vertex.

optional_outputs.name: per_edge_count
optional_outputs.description: Triangles containing each edge.

solution_semantics.objective: Count every size-three clique exactly once and materialize requested secondary outputs.
solution_semantics.exactness: The global count and requested participation counts are exact.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each unordered triple is counted and listed once.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering is required.

validation_rules: Every listed triple contains three distinct pairwise-adjacent vertices.
The sum of per-vertex counts equals three times the global count.
The sum of per-edge counts equals three times the global count.
edge_cases: Graphs with fewer than three vertices have count zero.
A complete n-vertex graph contains n choose 3 triangles.
Isolated vertices have per-vertex count zero.

spec.name: Graph Motif Counting
spec.problem_statement: Count occurrences of one or more supplied small structural patterns in a directed or undirected graph.

normalization: Remove self-loops unless explicitly present in a future motif extension.
Collapse parallel edges with identical direction into one edge.
Preserve edge direction for directed motifs.

problem_inputs.name: motifs
problem_inputs.constraints: nonempty array of small connected patterns
problem_inputs.description: Motif definitions using the same canonical graph format.

problem_inputs.name: induced
problem_inputs.description: Require each occurrence to contain exactly the motif edges among selected vertices.

problem_inputs.name: occurrence_identity
problem_inputs.description: Controls whether automorphism-equivalent embeddings are counted separately.

problem_inputs.name: list_instances
problem_inputs.description: Materialize matching data-graph vertex mappings.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit_per_motif
problem_inputs.description: Maximum listed instances for each motif; counts remain exhaustive.

required_outputs.name: count_by_motif
required_outputs.description: Exact occurrence count under the selected identity semantics.

required_outputs.name: instances_complete_by_motif
required_outputs.description: Whether every requested instance was materialized.

optional_outputs.name: instances_by_motif
optional_outputs.description: Mappings from motif vertices to data-graph vertices.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_participation
optional_outputs.description: Occurrence participation counts.

solution_semantics.objective: Count subgraphs isomorphic to each motif under direction, inducedness, and occurrence-identity settings.
solution_semantics.exactness: Counts are exact; listing may be capped but must disclose completeness.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Occurrences follow occurrence_identity and are otherwise unique.
solution_semantics.ordering: Result ordering is irrelevant; directed edge orientation is significant.

validation_rules: Every instance preserves motif adjacency and direction.
Induced instances contain no additional edges among mapped vertices.
Counts account for motif automorphisms according to occurrence_identity.
edge_cases: A motif larger than the data graph has count zero.
Isomorphic motif definitions may produce identical counts but remain separately identified.
Disconnected motif definitions are rejected in version 1.

spec.name: Subgraph Isomorphism and Pattern Matching
spec.problem_statement: Find injective mappings from the vertices of a query graph to a data graph that preserve required edges, direction, and requested attribute predicates.

normalization: Preserve query and data edge direction.
Preserve parallel-edge identity when predicates distinguish edges.
Do not silently remove self-loops used by the query.

problem_inputs.name: query_graph
problem_inputs.description: Pattern graph expressed using canonical_edge_list_v1.

problem_inputs.name: induced
problem_inputs.description: Require mapped vertices to have no extra data edges beyond query edges.

problem_inputs.name: vertex_predicates
problem_inputs.description: Declarative constraints on mapped vertex type, label, or attributes.

problem_inputs.name: edge_predicates
problem_inputs.description: Declarative constraints on mapped edge type, weight, timestamp, or attributes.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized mappings.

required_outputs.name: matches
required_outputs.description: Injective query-to-data vertex mappings.

required_outputs.name: returned_count
required_outputs.description: Number of materialized mappings.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all qualifying mappings were found.

optional_outputs.name: total_count
optional_outputs.description: Exact number of mappings when known.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate all injective mappings satisfying structural, directional, inducedness, and attribute constraints.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every returned mapping is exact; complete=true requires exhaustive matching.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Distinct query-to-data mappings are distinct results, even when query automorphisms map to the same data vertex set.
solution_semantics.ordering: Mapping order is irrelevant.

validation_rules: Mappings are injective.
Every query edge has a matching data edge with correct direction and predicates.
Induced matches contain no prohibited extra mapped edges.
All vertex predicates hold.
edge_cases: A query larger than the data graph has no matches.
An empty query has one empty mapping by convention.
Query automorphisms may yield multiple mappings to one data vertex set.

spec.name: Temporal Motif Mining
spec.problem_statement: Count occurrences of a small ordered edge pattern whose matched events occur in the required order within a bounded time window.

normalization: Normalize all edge timestamps to UTC epoch seconds without changing order.
Preserve parallel temporal events as distinct edge IDs.
Preserve edge direction.
Reject missing or invalid timestamps.

problem_inputs.name: temporal_motif
problem_inputs.description: Small graph pattern whose edges have a required total or partial temporal order.

problem_inputs.name: maximum_duration_seconds
problem_inputs.description: Maximum last-edge minus first-edge time for an occurrence.

problem_inputs.name: allow_equal_timestamps
problem_inputs.description: Whether consecutively ordered motif edges may share a timestamp.

problem_inputs.name: temporal_induced
problem_inputs.description: Reject occurrences with additional participating-vertex events inside the occurrence window.

problem_inputs.name: list_instances
problem_inputs.description: Materialize matched edge-event sequences.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum listed instances; the total count remains exhaustive.

required_outputs.name: occurrence_count
required_outputs.description: Exact number of temporal motif occurrences.

required_outputs.name: instances_complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all instances were materialized when listing was requested.

optional_outputs.name: instances
optional_outputs.description: Matched vertices, ordered edge IDs, timestamps, and occurrence duration.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_participation
optional_outputs.description: Occurrences involving each data vertex.

solution_semantics.objective: Count structurally valid event sequences satisfying motif order, duration, equality, and temporal-inducedness semantics.
solution_semantics.exactness: The occurrence count is exact; listing may be capped.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: A distinct ordered tuple of edge-event IDs is a distinct occurrence.
solution_semantics.ordering: Temporal order is semantically significant.

validation_rules: Each instance preserves motif structure and direction.
Event timestamps satisfy the declared order.
Occurrence duration does not exceed maximum_duration_seconds.
No temporal-inducedness violation exists when enabled.
edge_cases: No events yields count zero.
Equal-timestamp events are rejected from strict order positions unless allowed.
Repeated edges between the same endpoints remain distinct events.

correctness: count agreement with exhaustive temporal matcher

spec.name: Disjoint Community Detection
spec.problem_statement: Partition all graph vertices into nonoverlapping communities that maximize a declared within-community quality function.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops unless the selected quality definition explicitly retains them.
Collapse parallel edges by summing weights; use unit weights in unweighted mode.

problem_inputs.name: quality_function
problem_inputs.description: Mathematical quality objective optimized by the partition.

problem_inputs.name: resolution
problem_inputs.description: Resolution parameter controlling the preferred community scale.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use unit edge values or nonnegative input weights.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether global optimality is required or a locally optimized partition is acceptable.

required_outputs.name: community_by_vertex
required_outputs.description: Exactly one community assignment for every input vertex.

required_outputs.name: community_count
required_outputs.description: Number of nonempty communities.

required_outputs.name: quality_score
required_outputs.description: Recomputed selected objective value.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven.

optional_outputs.name: community_statistics
optional_outputs.description: Size, internal edge value, boundary edge value, and density.

optional_outputs.name: hierarchy
optional_outputs.description: Intermediate or multilevel partitions when meaningful.

solution_semantics.objective: Maximize the selected partition quality over disjoint, exhaustive vertex assignments.
solution_semantics.exactness: Heuristic mode returns a feasible partition without claiming a global optimum.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Community identifiers are arbitrary; partitions equal up to identifier permutation are equivalent.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering is required.

validation_rules: Every vertex belongs to exactly one nonempty community.
No unknown vertex appears.
Recomputed quality equals quality_score within declared numeric tolerance.
edge_cases: An empty graph has no communities.
Isolated vertices must still receive exactly one assignment.
Multiple partitions may have the same quality score.

correctness: objective gap when an exact oracle is available

spec.name: Centrality and Influential-Node Mining
spec.problem_statement: Compute a declared centrality score for graph vertices and rank the most structurally influential vertices under that definition.

normalization: Preserve direction when requested by the measure.
Remove self-loops unless the selected centrality definition includes them.
Collapse parallel edges according to the selected weight semantics.

problem_inputs.name: centrality_measure
problem_inputs.description: Mathematical definition used to score vertices.

problem_inputs.name: direction_mode
problem_inputs.description: How directed edges contribute where the measure supports direction.

problem_inputs.name: weight_semantics
problem_inputs.description: Interpret edge weights as ignored, connection strength, or path distance.

problem_inputs.name: top_k
problem_inputs.description: Optionally return only the highest-ranked vertices while retaining score-completeness metadata.

problem_inputs.name: measure_parameters
problem_inputs.description: Definition-level values such as PageRank damping, Katz alpha and beta, normalization, or a restricted source set.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether approximation or sampling is permitted for expensive measures.

required_outputs.name: ranked_vertices
required_outputs.description: Vertex ID, score, and rank ordered by descending influence.

required_outputs.name: score_definition
required_outputs.description: Resolved measure, direction, weight, normalization, and parameter semantics.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every vertex was scored and ranking was not truncated.

optional_outputs.name: converged
optional_outputs.description: Whether an iterative measure met its convergence criterion.

optional_outputs.name: error_or_sampling_bound
optional_outputs.description: Known numerical or statistical bound for approximate scores.

solution_semantics.objective: Score and rank vertices exactly according to the selected centrality definition and resolved parameters.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exactness is measure-specific; iterative and approximate methods must disclose convergence or bounds.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each scored vertex appears once.
solution_semantics.ordering: Descending score with a stable vertex-ID tie break for reproducibility.

validation_rules: Scores are recomputable from score_definition within numeric tolerance.
Every returned vertex exists in the graph.
Ranks are monotonic by score and ties follow the stated policy.
Weight values satisfy the chosen semantics.
edge_cases: Disconnected graphs require explicitly defined closeness behavior.
Dangling vertices require explicitly defined PageRank redistribution.
Tied scores are permitted.
An empty graph produces an empty ranking.

spec.name: Personalized PageRank and Random Walk with Restart
spec.problem_statement: Given one or more seed vertices, compute each vertex's steady-state visitation probability under a random walk that restarts to the seed distribution with fixed probability, and rank vertices by that score relative to the seeds.

normalization: Preserve direction unless undirected_projection is requested.
Remove self-loops unless self_loop_policy keeps them.
Collapse parallel edges by summing nonnegative weights; use unit weight when weight_mode=unweighted.
Handle dangling vertices (zero out-degree) per the declared dangling_policy.

problem_inputs.name: seed_vertices
problem_inputs.constraints: nonempty; weights nonnegative and not all zero
problem_inputs.description: Restart distribution. A plain array means a uniform restart distribution over the listed vertices.

problem_inputs.name: restart_probability
problem_inputs.description: Probability of teleporting back to the seed distribution at each step (alpha).

problem_inputs.name: direction_mode
problem_inputs.description: Walk direction for directed input; incoming computes Personalized PageRank with respect to reverse edges.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use uniform or weighted transition probabilities out of each vertex.

problem_inputs.name: dangling_policy
problem_inputs.description: How probability mass at zero-out-degree vertices is redistributed.

problem_inputs.name: top_k
problem_inputs.description: Return only the highest-scoring vertices while retaining score-completeness metadata.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether power iteration to a convergence tolerance, or an approximate method (e.g. forward push, random walks) with disclosed error, is permitted.

problem_inputs.name: convergence_tolerance
problem_inputs.description: L1 residual threshold for declaring convergence in exact_or_converged mode.

problem_inputs.name: exclude_seeds_from_output
problem_inputs.description: Whether seed vertices themselves are omitted from ranked output.

required_outputs.name: ranked_vertices
required_outputs.description: Vertex ID, PPR/RWR score, and rank ordered by descending score.

required_outputs.name: restart_probability_used
required_outputs.description: Resolved alpha actually used.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every eligible vertex was scored and ranking was not truncated by top_k.

optional_outputs.name: converged
optional_outputs.description: Whether the iterative solver met convergence_tolerance.

optional_outputs.name: iterations
optional_outputs.description: Iterations or pushes performed.

optional_outputs.name: error_bound
optional_outputs.description: Disclosed per-vertex or aggregate error bound for approximate mode.

solution_semantics.objective: Compute the stationary distribution of the restart random walk defined by seed_vertices, restart_probability, direction_mode, and weight_mode, then rank vertices by that probability.
solution_semantics.exactness: exact_or_converged requires the L1 residual below convergence_tolerance; approximate mode must disclose its error_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each eligible vertex appears at most once.
solution_semantics.ordering: Descending score with a stable vertex-ID tie break.

validation_rules: Scores sum to 1 over all vertices (or within numerical tolerance) before any top_k truncation.
Scores are non-negative.
Every seed vertex exists in the normalized graph.
Recomputing scores from score_definition and the normalized transition matrix matches reported values within tolerance.
Dangling-vertex mass is redistributed exactly as declared by dangling_policy.
edge_cases: A seed vertex with no outgoing edges under direction_mode still receives restart mass.
Seed weights that do not sum to one are normalized before use.
An isolated seed vertex in an otherwise edgeless graph places all mass on itself.
restart_probability close to 1 makes the result nearly identical to the seed distribution; close to 0 makes it close to global PageRank.

correctness: L1/L2 score error versus a power-iteration oracle
performance: queries per second for repeated single-seed queries

spec.name: Maximum Flow and Minimum s-t Cut
spec.problem_statement: Given a directed capacitated graph and designated source and sink vertices, compute a maximum feasible flow from source to sink and a minimum-capacity edge set whose removal disconnects source from sink.

normalization: Treat edge weight as capacity; reject negative capacity.
Collapse parallel edges between the same ordered pair by summing capacity.
Treat an undirected edge request as two opposite directed edges with equal capacity.
Remove self-loops; they never contribute to an s-t flow or cut.

problem_inputs.name: source
problem_inputs.description: Flow source vertex.

problem_inputs.name: sink
problem_inputs.description: Flow sink vertex.

problem_inputs.name: capacity_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use declared edge weights or treat every edge as unit capacity.

problem_inputs.name: vertex_capacities
problem_inputs.description: Optional per-vertex capacity for vertex-connectivity-style cuts; null means edge-only capacities.

problem_inputs.name: return_cut_side
problem_inputs.description: Whether to return the source-side vertex partition induced by the minimum cut.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether an approximate max-flow value with a disclosed bound is permitted.

required_outputs.name: max_flow_value
required_outputs.description: Value of the maximum feasible source-to-sink flow.

required_outputs.name: min_cut_value
required_outputs.description: Total capacity of the minimum s-t cut; equals max_flow_value by the max-flow min-cut theorem.

required_outputs.name: min_cut_edges
required_outputs.description: Edges crossing from the source side to the sink side of a minimum cut.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven.

optional_outputs.name: flow_assignment
optional_outputs.description: Feasible flow value on each edge satisfying capacity and conservation constraints.

optional_outputs.name: source_side_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Vertices reachable from source in the residual graph at optimality.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified relative or additive gap for an approximate result.

solution_semantics.objective: Maximize total flow leaving source subject to capacity and conservation constraints; the minimum cut is any minimum-capacity edge set separating source from sink.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true and max_flow_value == min_cut_value within tolerance.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Multiple minimum cuts may exist; return one unless alternates are explicitly requested.
solution_semantics.ordering: Not applicable; outputs are a value, an edge set, and optionally a flow assignment.

validation_rules: flow_assignment, when returned, satisfies 0 <= flow <= capacity on every edge and conservation at every non-terminal vertex.
min_cut_edges all cross from the source side to the sink side and their capacity sum equals min_cut_value.
max_flow_value equals min_cut_value within numeric tolerance.
Removing min_cut_edges leaves no directed path from source to sink.
edge_cases: No directed path exists from source to sink: max_flow_value is zero and min_cut_edges is empty.
Source and sink are the same vertex is rejected as invalid input.
Disconnected or zero-capacity edges do not affect optimality but may affect returned flow_assignment sparsity.
Multiple minimum cuts of equal value may exist; any one is acceptable unless the caller requests the source-side-maximal or sink-side-maximal canonical cut.

correctness: flow value agreement with exact oracle

spec.name: Butterfly Counting and (alpha,beta)-Core Decomposition on Bipartite Graphs
spec.problem_statement: Given a bipartite graph, count butterflies (complete 2x2 bicliques, i.e. (2,2)-bicliques) globally and per vertex/edge, and optionally decompose the graph into (alpha,beta)-cores by butterfly-based degeneracy.

normalization: Reject edges whose endpoints share the same declared side.
Remove self-loops (impossible in valid bipartite input; reject if present).
Collapse parallel edges between the same pair to one edge.
Every vertex must have a side label in {left, right}; isolated vertices on either side are retained.

problem_inputs.name: mode
problem_inputs.description: Return a global count, per-vertex/per-edge participation counts, or a full (alpha,beta)-core decomposition.

problem_inputs.name: alpha
problem_inputs.description: Left-side degeneracy parameter when mode=alpha_beta_core; null means decompose for all feasible alpha.

problem_inputs.name: beta
problem_inputs.description: Right-side degeneracy parameter when mode=alpha_beta_core; null means decompose for all feasible beta.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether a sampling-based approximate butterfly count with a disclosed bound is permitted.

required_outputs.name: butterfly_count
required_outputs.description: Total number of distinct butterflies (unordered 2x2 complete bipartite subgraphs) in the graph.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether the count/decomposition covers the entire input graph without sampling truncation.

optional_outputs.name: per_vertex_butterfly_count
optional_outputs.description: Butterflies each vertex participates in; present when mode=per_vertex.

optional_outputs.name: per_edge_butterfly_count
optional_outputs.description: Butterflies each edge (as a wedge pair) participates in; present when mode=per_edge.

optional_outputs.name: alpha_beta_core_assignment
optional_outputs.description: Per-vertex maximal (alpha,beta) coordinates; present when mode=alpha_beta_core.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified relative error bound for an approximate count.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate or count every 4-cycle formed by two left vertices and two right vertices that are all pairwise connected (a butterfly), with no induced-subgraph requirement beyond the four required edges.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires every butterfly to be counted exactly once; approximate mode must disclose its bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each unordered set of 2 left + 2 right vertices forming a butterfly is counted once regardless of discovery order.
solution_semantics.ordering: Not applicable for global count; per_vertex and per_edge outputs are unordered maps.

validation_rules: butterfly_count recomputes from the normalized bipartite adjacency via independent wedge-based counting.
Sum of per_vertex_butterfly_count over one side, divided by 2, is internally consistent with butterfly_count.
alpha_beta_core_assignment vertices retain at least alpha (left) or beta (right) butterfly-degree within their assigned core.
No edge with same-side endpoints is present in the normalized graph.
edge_cases: A graph with no 4-cycles has butterfly_count zero.
A complete bipartite graph K(m,n) has the closed-form C(m,2)*C(n,2) butterflies, usable as a correctness check.
Isolated vertices contribute zero to every count.
alpha=1,beta=1 core reduces to vertices with degree >= 1 on each side that share at least one butterfly.

correctness: exact count agreement with brute-force wedge oracle on small/medium fixtures

spec.name: Group Steiner Tree
spec.problem_statement: Given an edge-weighted graph and a collection of potentially overlapping vertex groups, find a minimum-weight connected subtree that includes at least one vertex from every group.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges by keeping the minimum nonnegative weight.
Reject negative edge weights.

problem_inputs.name: groups
problem_inputs.constraints: at least one group; every group nonempty; groups may overlap and may share vertices with each other
problem_inputs.description: Each group must contribute at least one vertex to the returned tree.

problem_inputs.name: required_vertices
problem_inputs.description: Optional vertices (e.g. single-terminal requirements) that must appear in the tree regardless of group membership; equivalent to singleton groups.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether a certified-approximation result (e.g. a 2-approximation) with a disclosed ratio is permitted instead of an exact minimum.

required_outputs.name: tree_edges
required_outputs.description: Edges forming the returned connected subtree.

required_outputs.name: tree_weight
required_outputs.description: Sum of weights of tree_edges.

required_outputs.name: selected_vertices
required_outputs.description: Vertices spanned by tree_edges, including at least one representative per group.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven.

optional_outputs.name: group_representatives
optional_outputs.description: The specific vertex chosen to satisfy each group index, when a group has multiple qualifying vertices in the tree.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified worst-case ratio to optimal for an approximate result.

solution_semantics.objective: Minimize tree_weight over connected subtrees of the normalized graph that contain at least one vertex from every group in groups and every vertex in required_vertices.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true; approximate mode must disclose approximation_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Multiple minimum-weight trees may exist; return one unless alternates are explicitly requested.
solution_semantics.ordering: tree_edges and selected_vertices are unordered sets.

validation_rules: tree_edges forms a single connected acyclic subgraph (a tree) in the normalized graph.
Every group in groups has at least one vertex in selected_vertices.
Every vertex in required_vertices is in selected_vertices.
tree_weight equals the sum of tree_edges weights.
Reported optimal=true matches independent verification against an exhaustive oracle on small fixtures.
edge_cases: A single group containing the whole vertex set reduces to the cheapest single vertex, with an empty tree_edges and tree_weight zero.
Groups that already share a common vertex may be satisfied by a single-vertex tree.
Disconnected graphs where some group is entirely unreachable from another group make the instance infeasible; this must be reported rather than silently returning a partial tree.
Overlapping groups may be satisfied by the same vertex without double-selecting it.

correctness: tree-weight agreement with exact oracle on small/medium fixtures

spec.name: Influence Maximization under Diffusion Models
spec.problem_statement: Given a directed graph with edge-level influence probabilities and a declared stochastic diffusion model, select a seed set of a given size that maximizes the expected number of vertices eventually activated.

normalization: Treat edge weight as the independent-cascade activation probability, or as linear-threshold edge weight depending on diffusion_model.
Reject edge weight outside [0,1] for independent_cascade.
Collapse parallel edges per diffusion_model's combination rule (declared explicitly, since probabilities do not sum like capacities).
Remove self-loops; they do not affect diffusion.

problem_inputs.name: diffusion_model
problem_inputs.description: Stochastic process governing how activation spreads from seeds.

problem_inputs.name: seed_set_size
problem_inputs.description: Number of seed vertices to select (the budget k).

problem_inputs.name: vertex_thresholds
problem_inputs.description: Per-vertex activation thresholds for linear_threshold; null means thresholds are drawn uniformly at random per the model's standard definition.

problem_inputs.name: estimation_method
problem_inputs.description: Technique used to estimate expected spread while selecting seeds.

problem_inputs.name: approximation_guarantee
problem_inputs.description: Target multiplicative approximation ratio to the optimal expected spread (e.g. 1 - 1/e for the standard greedy guarantee).

problem_inputs.name: failure_probability
problem_inputs.description: Allowed probability that the returned seed set fails to meet approximation_guarantee, under the sampling method's own randomness.

required_outputs.name: seed_set
required_outputs.description: Selected seed vertices, with cardinality equal to seed_set_size.

required_outputs.name: expected_spread
required_outputs.description: Estimated expected number of activated vertices when diffusion starts from seed_set.

required_outputs.name: guarantee_met
required_outputs.description: Whether the returned seed_set is certified to meet approximation_guarantee under failure_probability.

optional_outputs.name: marginal_gains
optional_outputs.description: Estimated marginal expected-spread gain contributed by each seed, in selection order.

optional_outputs.name: sample_count
optional_outputs.description: Number of reverse-reachable sets or Monte Carlo simulations used to produce the estimate.

optional_outputs.name: confidence_interval
optional_outputs.description: Statistical interval around expected_spread for the estimation method used.

solution_semantics.objective: Choose seed_set of size seed_set_size maximizing expected_spread under diffusion_model, where expected_spread is the expectation over the model's randomness of the number of eventually-activated vertices.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact computation of expected_spread is #P-hard in general; guarantee_met=true requires the disclosed approximation_guarantee and failure_probability to hold under the estimation_method's established theoretical bounds.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: seed_set contains each vertex at most once.
solution_semantics.ordering: seed_set has no required output ordering unless marginal_gains is returned, in which case order reflects the greedy selection sequence.

validation_rules: seed_set has exactly seed_set_size distinct vertices that exist in the graph.
expected_spread is non-negative and at most the total vertex count.
Re-estimating expected_spread for the returned seed_set via independent simulation falls within confidence_interval or a stated tolerance.
vertex_thresholds, when supplied, are all within [0,1] for linear_threshold.
edge_cases: seed_set_size greater than or equal to the vertex count makes expected_spread equal to the vertex count.
A graph with no edges gives expected_spread equal to seed_set_size regardless of diffusion_model.
All edge probabilities zero under independent_cascade gives expected_spread equal to seed_set_size.
Disconnected components require seeds to be distributed to maximize total spread, not concentrated in one component.

correctness: expected-spread estimate agreement with high-sample-count simulation oracle
guarantee validity under disclosed sampling parameters
performance: reverse-reachable sets or simulations per second

spec.name: Bipartite Matching and Linear Assignment
spec.problem_statement: Given a bipartite graph, find a matching (a set of edges with no shared endpoints) that is optimal under a declared objective: maximum cardinality, maximum total weight, or minimum total cost.

normalization: Reject edges whose endpoints share the same declared side.
Reject self-loops (impossible in valid bipartite input).
Collapse parallel edges between the same pair by keeping the single best-objective weight.

problem_inputs.name: objective
problem_inputs.description: Maximize the number of matched pairs, maximize total matched weight, or minimize total matched cost.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: maximum_cardinality always behaves as unweighted; maximum_weight and minimum_cost require edge_weight.

problem_inputs.name: perfect_matching_required
problem_inputs.description: Whether every vertex on the smaller side (or both sides, if equal size) must be covered by the returned matching; infeasibility must be reported explicitly rather than returning a partial match.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: This problem is polynomial-time solvable; exact is the default, with approximate permitted only for very large instances with a disclosed bound.

required_outputs.name: matching_edges
required_outputs.description: Selected edges forming the matching; no two share a vertex.

required_outputs.name: matching_size
required_outputs.description: Number of matched pairs, equal to |matching_edges|.

required_outputs.name: objective_value
required_outputs.description: Total weight/cost of matching_edges under the declared objective (equal to matching_size for maximum_cardinality).

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven.

optional_outputs.name: unmatched_left_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Left-side vertices not covered by matching_edges.

optional_outputs.name: unmatched_right_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Right-side vertices not covered by matching_edges.

optional_outputs.name: feasible
optional_outputs.description: Whether a perfect matching exists, when perfect_matching_required=true.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified relative error bound for an approximate result.

solution_semantics.objective: Select a matching optimal under the declared objective: maximize |matching_edges| for maximum_cardinality, maximize total weight for maximum_weight, or minimize total weight for minimum_cost.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true; this problem admits polynomial-time exact algorithms (augmenting paths, Hungarian algorithm), so approximate mode is only for extreme scale and must disclose approximation_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each vertex appears in at most one entry of matching_edges.
solution_semantics.ordering: matching_edges is an unordered set.

validation_rules: matching_edges forms a valid matching (no two edges share an endpoint) in the normalized bipartite graph.
matching_size equals |matching_edges|.
objective_value recomputes exactly as the sum of matched edge weights (or equals matching_size for maximum_cardinality).
perfect_matching_required=true with feasible=true implies every vertex on the smaller (or both, if equal) side is covered; feasible=false must correspond to a provably infeasible instance.
edge_cases: An edgeless graph has matching_size zero and empty matching_edges.
A graph admitting a perfect matching must return one when perfect_matching_required=true.
Maximum matching size is bounded above by the smaller side's vertex count.
Negative weights under minimum_cost are valid input and must not be clamped to zero.

correctness: optimality agreement with an exact oracle (e.g. Hopcroft-Karp or Hungarian algorithm) on small/medium fixtures
performance: augmenting paths or auction rounds performed

spec.name: Transitive Closure and Reachability Indexing
spec.problem_statement: Given a directed graph, determine for queried vertex pairs whether the target is reachable from the source via a directed path, and optionally materialize or index full reachability to answer many such queries efficiently.

normalization: Collapse parallel directed edges between the same ordered pair to one edge.
Retain self-loops only insofar as every vertex already reaches itself by the reflexive convention; a self-loop does not change any reachability result.
Reject undirected input unless an explicit directed projection (both directions) is requested.

problem_inputs.name: query_mode
problem_inputs.description: Answer one (source,target) pair, a batch of pairs, or characterize reachability for every ordered pair.

problem_inputs.name: query_pairs
problem_inputs.constraints: required and nonempty for single_pair (exactly one entry) and batch_pairs
problem_inputs.description: List of {source, target} pairs to answer.

problem_inputs.name: build_index
problem_inputs.description: Whether to construct a reusable reachability index amortizing cost across future queries, versus a one-off traversal per query.

problem_inputs.name: enumerate_closure_edges
problem_inputs.description: For full_transitive_closure, whether to return every reachable (source,target) pair explicitly; only feasible when the result is small.

required_outputs.name: reachability_results
required_outputs.description: For single_pair/batch_pairs: {source, target, reachable} per queried pair, in query_pairs order.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every requested query (or, for full_transitive_closure, every ordered pair) was correctly resolved.

optional_outputs.name: reachable_pair_count
optional_outputs.description: Total number of reachable ordered pairs (including reflexive pairs); present for full_transitive_closure.

optional_outputs.name: transitive_closure_edges
optional_outputs.description: Explicit list of all reachable (source,target) pairs; returned only when enumerate_closure_edges=true and the result size is tractable.

optional_outputs.name: index_descriptor
optional_outputs.description: Opaque reference/metadata for a built reachability index, reusable by later single_pair/batch_pairs queries without rebuilding.

solution_semantics.objective: For each queried pair, determine whether target is reachable from source via a directed path of length >= 0 in the normalized graph (a vertex always reaches itself); full_transitive_closure characterizes this for every ordered pair.
solution_semantics.exactness: Reachability is always answered exactly; no approximate mode is defined for this problem.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: A repeated pair in query_pairs returns a consistent, identical result each time.
solution_semantics.ordering: reachability_results preserves the order of query_pairs.

validation_rules: Every reachable=true result is witnessed by at least one directed walk from source to target in the normalized graph.
Every reachable=false result has no directed walk from source to target, verifiable by exhaustive BFS/DFS on small/medium fixtures.
Every vertex is reachable from itself (reflexive case).
transitive_closure_edges, when returned, is consistent with reachable_pair_count.
edge_cases: source equals target returns reachable=true by the reflexive convention regardless of self-loops.
An edgeless graph has every non-reflexive pair unreachable.
Every pair of vertices within the same strongly connected component is mutually reachable.
full_transitive_closure on a graph where the closure is too large to enumerate must omit transitive_closure_edges and still return a correct reachable_pair_count with complete=true.

correctness: reachability agreement with exhaustive BFS/DFS oracle on small/medium fixtures
closure-edge-count consistency with transitive_closure_edges when both are returned
performance: amortized query time after index build

spec.name: Connected Components (Weakly and Strongly Connected)
spec.problem_statement: Partition all vertices into maximal groups such that every pair of vertices within a group is connected according to a declared connectivity definition: weak (undirected) connectivity, or strong (directed, mutual-reachability) connectivity.

normalization: Remove self-loops; they never change component membership.
Collapse parallel edges between the same pair to one edge.
When connectivity_mode=weakly_connected, treat every edge as undirected regardless of input direction.

problem_inputs.name: connectivity_mode
problem_inputs.description: Weak connectivity ignores edge direction; strong connectivity requires a directed path in both directions and is only meaningful (and may differ from weak) on a directed graph.

required_outputs.name: component_assignment
required_outputs.description: Component index assigned to every vertex.

required_outputs.name: component_count
required_outputs.description: Number of distinct components.

required_outputs.name: component_sizes
required_outputs.description: Vertex count of each component, indexed by component number.

optional_outputs.name: largest_component_id
optional_outputs.description: Component number with the most vertices.

optional_outputs.name: largest_component_size
optional_outputs.description: Vertex count of the largest component.

solution_semantics.objective: Assign every vertex a component_assignment such that two vertices share a component index if and only if they are connected under connectivity_mode, and components are maximal.
solution_semantics.exactness: This problem is always solved exactly; component identity is a decidable equivalence relation with no approximate mode.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each vertex belongs to exactly one component.
solution_semantics.ordering: Component indices are canonically numbered by ascending smallest-member vertex ID, so results are directly comparable across independent runs or implementations.

validation_rules: Two vertices share a component_assignment value if and only if they are connected under connectivity_mode in the normalized graph.
component_count equals the number of distinct values in component_assignment.
component_sizes[i] equals the number of vertices assigned to component i, and the entries sum to the total vertex count.
Component numbering follows the ascending-smallest-member-vertex-ID convention.
edge_cases: An isolated vertex forms its own singleton component.
An edgeless graph has every vertex in its own singleton component, so component_count equals the vertex count.
connectivity_mode=strongly_connected on a graph requested as an undirected projection degenerates to the same result as weakly_connected.
A self-loop does not merge a vertex with any other vertex.

correctness: component-assignment agreement with an exhaustive BFS/DFS (weak) or Tarjan/Kosaraju (strong) oracle on small/medium fixtures
